Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 500s on our dedicated pool (URGENT)

Quick triage (logs attached: redwood_ops_snapshot_0312.log):
- Observed: sustained GPU utilization on d-pool-7 at 96-99% from 07:48–08:22 PDT. Token latency spike correlates with an increase in KV cache churn and a higher tail latency for attention kernels on the quantized path.
- 5xxs: ~85% are 503/service-unavailable from our inference proxy; rest are 504/timeouts in the model runtime due to retry storms.
- Likely cause: a combination of a noisy tenant and an increase in long-context requests that evicted warm KV caches for other tenants on the same pool. We also saw a small kernel regression on one of the node images that increases execution time for long sequences (rolling out yesterday).

Immediate mitigations executed (09:05 PDT):
1) Throttled heavy batch windows from the noisy tenant (internal routing rule) to free headroom.
2) Enabled per-customer KV pinning for Crestline to reduce eviction churn (temporary override).
3) Rolled back the kernel image on 4 nodes where regression was visible.

Result: 09:12–09:25 PDT saw 5xxs drop to <0.5% and median token latency fall to ~125ms. We will continue monitoring for the next 6 hours.

Remaining asks / next steps:
- Karthik: can you validate whether the pinned KV cache increases memory usage in a way that would cause OOMs for other tenants? If so we will keep pinning but request burst approval.
- Ops: recommend scheduling a burst allocation for Crestline for the next 48 hours to cover unusual tails while we optimize (provision +10% headroom).
- Customer (Raj): we will prepare a short RCA and propose a permanent fix (model variant tuning + stricter cross-tenant isolation for d-pool-7).

Irene, marking this as incident type: reserved-throughput-pressure. I’ll add full logs to the incident page.

—Marissa
SRE, Dedicated Pools
